The intention of the F-35 is to shoot it down before it gets near.

Yeah, that's a nice intention and all, but combat has a way of throwing intentions out the window. The F-4 was intended to make all its kills with air-to-air missiles, so they didn't give it guns. When it went up against older Vietnamese Migs, the missiles and plane didn't work as advertised so they had to add a gun pod so the F-4's would stop getting shot down in dogfights.

The F-35 makes a similar over-reliance on new technology that hasn't been fully fleshed out. It has to see a plane before the plane sees it? That will only ever happen when the two planes are moving directly at each other... and the radar on the enemy plane isn't powerful enough to see the somewhat stealthy F-35 first. And then, if the F-35 opens its bays to fire missiles, it gives away its position and alerts the enemy plane to the threat, at which point it can do many different things to negate the missile or avoid it (the Su-27+ family uses a multitude of methods). Other than stealthiness, the Su-35 (and even less advanced aircraft) outclass the F-35 in every way, which means it will be absolutely worthless in a dogfight where its stealth doesn't matter.
